subject.title: Remove legacy tools.exec.security config in favor of tools.exec.mode

question: Should `tools.exec.mode` become the sole steady-state exec-policy config, including new mode values needed to preserve every shipped `security` plus `ask` combination?
rationale: Choosing the permanent mode vocabulary and migration mapping changes a command-execution security boundary and existing upgrade behavior; source inspection can identify failures but cannot determine which legacy postures maintainers intend to preserve as public contract.

options.title: Approve upgrade-safe mode migration
options.body: Make mode canonical, add only the values required for exact legacy semantics, fix the sandbox ask-only mapping, and require representative doctor plus runtime proof before landing.

options.title: Retain legacy keys temporarily
options.body: Keep security and ask supported until a smaller mode design can preserve every shipped combination without ambiguous migration behavior.

options.title: Fix CLI conflict first
options.body: Change current CLI writers to respect or replace mode now, while deferring removal and doctor migration to a separately approved compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Approve upgrade-safe mode migration
recommendation.body: Make mode canonical, add only the values required for exact legacy semantics, fix the sandbox ask-only mapping, and require representative doctor plus runtime proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide configuration and execution-policy compatibility choice, and the official repository maintainer is the strongest available final decision owner.
